Thanks Marissa — reviewed Acme's asks and your draft redlines. Summary of recommended positions below (tracked changes attached — Redwood_OrderForm_SuggestedLanguage.pdf):

1) Minimum commit definition
- Recommend defining "Minimum Commitment" as "Committed Spend per Contract Quarter" (i.e., dollars committed for each 3-month period).
- Unused credits: allow one-time limited carry-forward equal to 25% of the prior quarter's unused balance, but expire after the following quarter. This is a commercial concession but caps liability.

2) Net terms / payment schedule
- Our standard is Net 30. For strategic accounts we can offer Net 45 as a compromise. Net 60 exposes cash and credit risk; if Acme requires Net 60, propose adding a modest administrative fee (0.5% of invoice) for receivables >60 days or require a letter of credit / purchase order confirmation.
- Alternative: offer Net 60 on the condition of an agreed prepayment schedule (e.g., 50% prepay of first quarter) or a short-term credit review.

3) Invoicing cadence
- We can invoice quarterly in arrears and provide a consolidated invoice per quarter. Need to ensure finance can support consolidated billing across regions. Nikhil: confirm ERP mapping.

4) Taxes & withholding
- Standard position: Redwood will charge applicable taxes and provide tax invoices. For foreign withholding taxes, Redwood will not gross-up by default; propose to evaluate on a per-jurisdiction basis and include a tax-indemnity clause for the customer to provide documentation when taxes are withheld.

5) Late payment / remedies
- Recommend limited late fee language (1.5% per month) and suspend non-production accounts only after 30 days' written notice.

Please see attached PDF for exact redline text to paste into the Order Form. If we accept Net 60 with no additional mitigation, we should route to credit team for underwriting.

Happy to talk through on quick call.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference

Marissa / Laura — thanks for the quick turnaround and detailed commentary. A few notes from our side after reviewing the suggested language:

- Minimum commitment: the quarterly committed-spend approach is acceptable, but Acme requests that any carry-forward not expire if the customer is in an active contract term; propose that carry-forward credits remain usable for the remainder of the contract term rather than expiring after one quarter.
- Net terms: Acme's finance team strongly prefers Net 60 without administrative fees. If that's a hard constraint (i.e., Redwood cannot accept Net 60 without fee), please propose the minimal credit requirement or prepayment threshold required to qualify for Net 60 so we can take to our CFO.
- Invoicing: quarterly consolidated invoice is acceptable. Please include a sample invoice layout when you send the final Order Form so our AP knows mapping.
- Taxes: we'll provide tax residency certificates where required; please flag any jurisdictions where withholding may apply and the likely treatment.

If you can send the tracked Order Form with the redlines accepted where possible and comments next to the provisions where you need credit or finance inputs, we'll route to our CFO and legal for final sign-off. Also send DocuSign link when ready.
